title.narrative: NIHR Global Health Research Group on Vaccines to Control Respiratory Pathogens and AMR across Africa (VacAMR)

description.narrative:
AMR-attributable deaths (~1.3 million per year) are primarily due to respiratory infections (LRI). Annually, there are over 2 million lower respiratory infection (LRI) deaths globally, most commonly in sub-Saharan Africa (SSA). Streptococcus pneumoniae (Spn), RSV, and Hib are the leading causes of LRI deaths among children under 5. Antimicrobial-resistant Klebsiella pneumoniae is a leading cause of pneumonia and sepsis in newborns and vulnerable adults. Influenza virus, RSV, and Spn infections significantly drive antimicrobial use, thus fueling AMR. Deaths caused by AMR respiratory pathogens are vaccine-preventable.
This initiative proposes improving AMR control by preventing disease syndromes such as fever and pneumonia through a multimodal approach, including vaccine and non-vaccine interventions. Building upon previous NIHR-funded success, the project aims to tackle AMR through new strategic South-South partnerships involving KEMRI-Wellcome (Kenya), Malawi-Liverpool-Wellcome (Kamuzu University of Health Sciences), Navrongo Health Research Centre (Ghana), Nigeria Centre for Disease Control, and the Nigerian Institute of Medical Research.
Overall Aim: Africa-led transformation of public health approaches to controlling respiratory pathogens and AMR using multimodal vaccine and non-vaccine interventions.

i. Identify multimodal interventions to reduce AMR, develop the evidence base, co-create interventions, model impact, and prioritize methodologies.
ii. Accelerate the implementation of diagnostic approaches to support AMR intervention evaluation.
iii. Evaluate candidate immune markers of protection to support intervention and outcome evaluation.
iv. Strengthen evidence-to-policy translation.
v. Engage communities to evaluate AMR risk and identify behavior change interventions.
vi. Empower Africa-based leadership and innovation in AMR.
